question_record.context: A multi-stage security incident involving various malicious activities was observed. Initially, a suspicious file named `iy2orr1e.rrg.exe` was launched on the host `mb-adfs` by the account `gsmith`. This might have been an attempt to hide the use of a dual-purpose tool for malicious activities. Following this, there were signs of a system executable being renamed and possibly used for malicious purposes, code injection into processes, and an account sending phishing emails. The incident eventually led to malicious URL-containing emails being delivered and then removed.
question_record.question: Can you identify the recipient of the email messages containing the malicious URL that were removed after delivery?
solution: The host `mb-adfs` saw an attempt to hide the use of a dual-purpose tool.
A renamed Windows executable `powershell.exe` was launched, potentially for malicious activities.
Code injection was detected in a process belonging to an account with SID `S-1-5-21-561436748-3867387497-1732241745-3701`.
An internal user account `Nina Sullivan@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co` sent phishing emails within the organization, indicating possible account compromise.
Emails containing malicious URLs and sent to `santiago@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co` were removed after delivery.

32.name: Attempt to hide use of dual-purpose tool
32.description:
A known public tool, which could also be used for malicious reasons, was observed under an unexpected filename.
This might be an attempt to hide the usage of that tool for malicious purposes.

27.name: System executable renamed and launched
27.description: A Windows executable file that has been renamed was launched. Attackers might be attempting to use the executable to perform malicious activities, such as running malicious code or connecting to an attacker-controlled network address. By changing the path or file name of a system executable, attackers can avoid certain behavior-based detection technologies that rely on default paths and file names.

41.name: A process was injected with potentially malicious code
41.description:
A process has injected code into another process, indicating suspicious code being run in the target process memory. Injection is often used to hide malicious code execution within a trusted process. 
As a result, the target process may exhibit abnormal behaviors such as opening a listening port or connecting to a command and control server.

88.name: Internal phishing lexpaign
88.description: A user was observed to have sent phishing email from this device to recipients inside the organization. The user account might have been compromised in an attempt by an attacker to move laterally inside the organization. This alert was triggered based on a Microsoft Defender for Office 365 alert.
